items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Oh. J.J. and Kai. We traveled a lot and we had records and it was a remarkable group because of how well they organized it.

ctx.x: We were talking about the group with J.J. and Kai.

Oh. J.J. and Kai. We traveled a lot and we had records and it was a remarkable group because of how well they organized it. J.J. was — they were very different. Even — they played similarly but not, they’re really different if you listen. J.J. was smooth, controlled and Kai was sort of brash. But they were in the idiom and they were great foils for each other and they devised all these arrangements with mutes and everything. It was a terrific experience. And our last gig was at the 1956 Newport festival and we…
Yeah. You should be fulfilled just because — and it is interesting. It’s like we want our artists to be — we want them to suffer almost. It makes us feel better or something.
